evidence: resolv-conf-names-exactly-the-given-servers: manifests/dns_client.pp:8-12 passes $nameservers to class resolv_conf; saz-resolv_conf 8.0.1's template (read on the master) writes one 'nameserver <ns>' line per element and nothing else matching ^nameserver, so with the fixture [10.0.2.3] exactly 'nameserver 10.0.2.3' is what the code produces (clean node: 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8, applied: 10.0.2.3)

a-nameserver-is-added-by-hand: same lines 8-12; the action (append 'nameserver 9.9.9.9') matches its mutates declaration, and the read-only effect (grep of the file) shows the drift result, not the echo's output; it is the setup the node_agent run then corrects

names-resolve-through-the-given-server: lines 1-2 ('configures the DNS servers for the client') plus 8-12; dig without @server uses /etc/resolv.conf, so NOERROR with SERVER 10.0.2.3 shows the resolver goes through the given server (clean: SERVER 1.1.1.1). The mismatch varies the queried name to the reserved p8test.invalid, which must change the server's verdict to NXDOMAIN, a real verdict change and not a broken command; it failed as required
